name: When should I start design if I want to break ground next year?

mainEntity.name: How far in advance should I start custom home design and permitting if I want to start construction next year?
mainEntity.text: How far in advance should I start custom home design and permitting if I want to start construction next year?

acceptedAnswer.text: If the goal is to break ground next year, design should begin well before the desired start date because custom home preconstruction often takes longer than owners expect. The schedule includes feasibility review, schematic design, design development, engineering, energy documentation, permit preparation, plan check corrections, and final approval. Even a straightforward project can lose weeks if the first set of drawings is incomplete or if the site triggers extra review. Homeowners should back-schedule from the desired construction start date and add buffer time for corrections and consultant coordination. A strong builder will help sequence the design process so long-lead decisions are made early, such as structural systems, window packages, and major finish selections. Waiting until the last minute is the easiest way to miss the build window.
acceptedAnswer.description: Design should usually start many months before the intended build date because plans, engineering, corrections, and permit approvals can take longer than expected. For custom homes in Los Angeles, waiting until the last minute can push the start date back by months. Early site study and design coordination give the best chance of hitting a target groundbreaking window.
